title: I Made This Ridiculous Game with ChatGPT Astra, Suno & ElevenLabs
author: prompttheplanet
selftext:
Hey guys,

I wanted to see how far I could get building a fun, complete browser game with AI in a single day's worth of working time.

The result is **The Big Escape**. It took around 8 hours of my time to create.  
[https://playerbits.ai/game/the-big-escape/](https://playerbits.ai/game/the-big-escape/)

In the game, you're trying to escape a nightclub without spilling your beer while being chased by a fat woman who keeps getting fatter and faster.

I basically described what I wanted, tested everything, gave feedback, and kept iterating until I got what I wanted. You guys know the drill.

I built it primarily with **Codex Astra High**, plus **Blender, Suno, and ElevenLabs**.

I gave Astra access to Blender (free download) to create a lot of the visual assets. Suno handled all three background music tracks, and I generated the sound effects with ElevenLabs.

I used the free versions of Suno and ElevenLabs. I'm currently on the $100/month ChatGPT plan (for now). I upgraded temporarily.

A few things I learned by building it:

1. Start with a clear concept. Explain who the player controls, what they're trying to do, how they lose, how they score points, and what makes the game fun (or in this case, dumb).
2. Give Codex visual references. Show it the characters, setting, and art style you want. Approve a few samples before having it generate a bunch of assets.
3. Build in small steps. Get something playable first. Then improve movement, enemies, graphics, sound, and UI through focused requests.
4. Play it constantly. Screenshots and specific feedback like "the enemy gets stuck behind this plant" were much more useful than vague feedback.
5. Test mobile early. Touch controls, camera framing, performance, and audio need to be tested on a real phone.
6. Save working versions. Keep backups before major changes. I also had Codex document important decisions so future sessions could pick up where the previous one stopped.
7. Tell Codex where you're going to host the game. Give it the intended URL and hosting platform so it can prepare the deployment properly.

Would be curious to hear what you guys think.
